issues.legal_issue: The one-year limit for challenging a published list of trusts does not prevent revenue authorities from deciding a trust-status dispute brought by a third party that is not interested in the trust, absent the notice required to bind that third party.
material_facts: A statutory notification listed the land as trust property, and the village community later disputed that status before revenue authorities.
The community representative was a third party, not a trustee or a person claiming through a trustee.
The community representative did not file a civil suit within one year of the notification.
There was no material showing that the community representative had been given notice during the inquiry preceding publication of the list.
The revenue authorities decided that the land belonged to the village community, and the later civil suit was brought by the trust board.
issues.conclusion: The one-year limit did not prevent the revenue authorities from deciding the dispute. The explanation that could extend the notification’s effect to third parties was not shown to apply because it was not in force and, in any event, there was no evidence that the community representative had received the required notice.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 5(2) and 6(1) of the Wakf Act, 1954, read with the first proviso to Section 6(1), the one-year suit requirement governs disputes between the Board, a mutawalli, or a person interested in the trust; “interested therein” means interested in the trust, not merely interested in the property. The Court applied Board of Muslim Wakfs, Rajasthan v. Radha Kishan, which relied on Sirrah Ha Khan v. The Sunni Central Board of Wakf, U.P., and distinguished Sayyed Ali v. A.P. Wakf Board because that dispute concerned the Board and persons claiming through the mutawalli. The 1984 Explanation could extend the effect to a third party interested in the property only if it applied and that person had received notice during the Section 4 inquiry; the Court noted that no commencement date had been issued and that no such notice was established.

predicates.third_party_property_dispute_before_reve: A person who is not interested in the trust and does not claim through its trustee disputes the trust’s claim to property before a revenue authority.
predicates.third_party_given_inquiry_notice: The third party received notice during the inquiry preceding publication of the property list.
predicates.explanation_not_in_force: The explanation extending the effect of the property list to third parties was not in force.

issues.definition: When a third party disputes trust status before a revenue authority and either did not receive inquiry notice or the extension was not in force, the authority may determine trust status.

issues.legal_issue: A civil suit challenging a revenue determination concerning village land is barred when the land is recorded as being used for the benefit or common purposes of the village community.
material_facts: The village community challenged the trust board’s claim before revenue authorities.
The revenue records showed the village panchayat as owner and showed the land being used for common village purposes.
The revenue authorities decided the dispute in favour of the village community.
The trust board later brought a civil suit seeking a declaration of ownership and possession.
issues.conclusion: The land fell within the definition of village common land and not within the exclusion for land not recorded as used for the village community. The statutory bar therefore applied, and the civil suit was barred.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 2(g) of the Punjab Village Common Lands (Regulation) Act, 1961, land described in the revenue records and used for the benefit or common purposes of the village community falls within village common land; the exclusion in clause (v) applies where the records do not show that use. Section 13 bars the civil suit in this case because the land was village common land and the revenue authorities had decided the dispute.

predicates.civil_suit_challenging_village_land_dete: A party brings a civil suit challenging a revenue determination concerning land claimed as village land.
predicates.revenue_records_show_community_use: The revenue records show that the land is used for the benefit or common purposes of the village community.

issues.definition: When a civil suit challenges a revenue determination concerning village land and the revenue records show community use, the civil suit is barred.
